/01

Flutter · Windows, Android & iOS · Interview prep

StackSquire

For sale · $10K

Level up your code. Conquer your interviews.

A gamified, offline-first interview-prep app for entry-level and junior software engineers — native Windows, Android, and iOS apps from one Flutter codebase. It blends coding practice, daily habits, spaced repetition, and RPG progression: skill trees, XP, quests, and boss battles.

  • 40K+ lines of Dart and 645 automated tests in CI: six learning paths, 50 lessons, 271 questions, 39 coding and debugging challenges, 11 visualizations, and mock interviews.
  • A sandboxed Python 3 interpreter written in pure Dart — output verified against CPython, with step, memory, and recursion limits — so learners run and grade real code offline.
  • Event-sourced progress with deterministic replay; Firebase sync across devices never awards duplicate XP, and a Cloud Function re-runs the same rules engine to verify rewards.
  • Real-World Developer Mode: fix a failing build, refactor to complexity targets, review a pull request, and write unit tests graded by mutation testing.

    Progress is event-sourced: the app never stores “XP = 5,713”. It stores what you did, and the same pure-Dart rules turn that history into state — on the device and again on the server.

    1. 01 · ActLearning actionAnswer, review, solve, or battle.
    2. 02 · RecordImmutable eventUUID, UTC time, local date, device ID, and content version.
    3. 03 · ReplayDeterministic reducerXP, levels, mastery, streaks, quests, and readiness from history.
    4. 04 · SyncTwo checksDevices · FirebaseMerge without duplicate XPServer · Cloud FunctionSame engine, compiled to JavaScript

    → events append only⇄ background sync✓ server-verified level and XP

    /02

    Bremerton Sports Car Club · Event platform

    BSCC Paddock

    Pre-release

    Race day, even when the signal isn’t.

    An event-management platform for a motorsport club’s autocross program: registration, payments, waivers, check-in, worker assignments, and live timing — built to keep working at a track with unreliable internet.

    • All six delivery phases built: an Android app (Kotlin, Jetpack Compose, Hilt, Room), a Firebase backend, and a Python bridge for the timing laptop.
    • Clients never decide money, capacity, or permissions: TypeScript Cloud Functions validate input, re-check access, and write an audit record in one transaction.
    • Offline-first race day: check-in by QR code or kiosk, waivers, tech inspection, and cash queue in a durable outbox and sync exactly once.
    • Stripe PaymentIntents with signature-verified webhooks, double-charge protection, and refunds; versioned scoring with audited timing corrections.
    • 450+ automated tests across Android, Cloud Functions, security rules, and the bridge, run in CI against the Firebase emulators.
    KotlinJetpack ComposeHiltRoomFirestoreCloud FunctionsTypeScriptStripePython

        /03

        CS 499 Capstone · Collaborative productivity

        MultiTasked

        Source on GitHub

        A shared place to keep the work moving.

        A collaborative Android task manager for shared projects and everyday life — boards people can create, share, and join, with real-time sync and a grocery mode that totals a list.

        • Jetpack Compose UI with Kotlin Coroutines and Firebase real-time synchronization.
        • Hash-generated list-sharing IDs and Android deep links that route users to the right destination across lifecycle states.
        • MVVM with immutable UI state, typed actions, input validation, reusable composables, and testable dependencies.
        • Custom merge sort and a heap-based priority queue for due-date and urgency sorting, run on background coroutines.
        • A separate offline Room/SQLite workspace with relational data, indexed queries, transactional updates, and migrations.
        • Design, algorithm, and database enhancements documented in a public ePortfolio with code review and automated test evidence.
        KotlinJetpack ComposeCoroutinesFirebaseRoomSQLiteMVVM

            An MVVM stack with one-way data flow: typed actions go in, immutable UI state comes out, and the repository decides whether data lives in the shared cloud or the offline workspace.
